newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM may ask parliament for more flood funds.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM may ask parliament for more flood funds.

text.p: Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz may seek a budget revision in order to create more funds for the flood relief programme, the government spokeswoman said on Friday.

"On Thursday the Premier asked the finance ministry to analyse and present their conclusions (about whether to ask parliament to alter the budget), but no decisions have been made yet," Aleksandra Jakubowska told Reuters.
She said a decision could be made as early as on Friday, but did not give any further details. The finance ministry was not immediately available for comment.

Late on Thursday the government, which has been criticised by the media for its handling of the flood crisis, carved out 500 million zlotys ($151.3 million) from various budget reserves to help victims of the flooding, which had claimed at least 23 lives.
Jakubowska also said that the prime minister activated state food reserves, which were now available for use to regional governors if needed.
"There are (sufficient) food reserves in Poland, but not in every place, so there is no need for (additional) food imports," she said.
The week-long flood displaced thousands of people and put more than 3,500 square km of the country underwater -- roughly one percent of Poland's surface area.
